items.author: MsftSecIntel
items.text:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence’s analysis of the active campaign abusing ScreenConnect to target managed service providers (MSPs) details how the remote support application is used to deploy the worm SCKit and install additional unauthorized clients. https://t.co/AbbE5BoAR8

SCKit is a malware toolkit that establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and registry Run entries and deploys RelayTrap, a component designed to deliver a malicious payload to technicians' workstations when they connect for support.

Read the blog for analysis, indicators of compromise, Microsoft Defender XDR detections and hunting queries, and mitigation guidance covering technician client updates, removal of toolkit persistence, and revocation of exposed sessions.

items.author: DarkReading
items.text:
Meet Artex: The agentic AI pen-testing tool fueling a wave of attacks.

Published to GitHub as a legitimate framework in July, a swath of attackers have abused Artex, from Chinese state-linked Storm-0940 to a financially motivated Cambodia-based cluster, Storm-3358.

None of the underlying tradecraft is new. Password spraying, credential stuffing, supply chain pivoting: This is familiar territory. What has changed is who can execute it, and how fast. Researchers also note that many Artex users show weak operational security despite the tool's sophistication, a gap that suggests the bar for who can pull off sophisticated cyberattacks keeps dropping.

https://t.co/HE1Z5U5Ewf

#Cybersecurity #ThreatIntelligence #AI #InfoSec

items.author: MsftSecIntel
items.text:
A model backdoor embeds hidden behavior that stays dormant until a trigger appears. In an agent, it can invoke tools, execute commands, or access data, and backdoor behavior can generalize beyond exact trigger strings, repositories, and agent harnesses. https://t.co/DNg23W8t0Z

Two studies of the post-training supply chain, from Microsoft Defender Research and the Microsoft AI Red Team, examine poisoned fine-tuning datasets and backdoored open-weight checkpoints. Their findings support Satya Nadella's argument that trustworthy enterprise AI requires independent observability and controls that sit outside the model.

Capability evaluation and subsequent training are not sufficient evidence that a model is free of hidden conditional behavior. Read the blog for the full findings and guidance on controls over training-data pipelines, model adoption, and tools.
